title: Chapter 6 Quiz: Sequence Modeling & NLP
description: Test your grasp of word embeddings, RNNs, LSTMs, the Attention mechanism, and Transformer architectures.

questions.question: What is the primary function of Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) tokenization in modern NLP?
options: Splitting text into frequent subword units to balance vocabulary size with out-of-vocabulary handling
questions.explanation: Subword tokenization like BPE iteratively merges frequent character pairs, allowing handling of unseen words via known sub-tokens.

questions.question: What geometric property characterizes dense word embeddings like Word2Vec and GloVe?
options: Words with similar semantic contexts are situated close to one another in vector space
Vectors only contain binary 0 and 1 values
Vector lengths correspond to word length in characters
questions.explanation: Word embeddings map semantic similarity into geometric proximity in dense multi-dimensional space.

questions.question: Standard feedforward neural networks can natively process variable-length text sentences without fixed padding or truncating.
questions.explanation: False. Dense MLPs require a fixed input dimension. Sequence models like RNNs or Transformers handle variable lengths.

questions.question: In a vanilla Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), what state is passed sequentially from timestep t-1 to timestep t?
questions.explanation: The hidden state h_t acts as the network's short-term memory, carrying context across sequential steps.

questions.question: Why do vanilla RNNs struggle to learn long-range dependencies across long paragraphs?
options: They only work on Spanish text
Vanishing and exploding gradients during Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT)
questions.explanation: Repeated matrix multiplications across time cause gradients to vanish or explode, wiping out long-term historical context.

questions.question: Which component in an LSTM acts as the linear, unimpeded 'information highway' carrying long-term memory?
questions.explanation: The Cell State runs straight down the LSTM chain with only minor linear interactions, mitigating vanishing gradients.

questions.question: How many gating mechanisms exist inside a standard LSTM cell?
questions.explanation: An LSTM has three gates: the Forget Gate, the Input Gate, and the Output Gate.

questions.question: The Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) simplifies the LSTM by merging the cell state and hidden state, using only two gates (Reset and Update).
questions.explanation: True. GRUs combine cell and hidden states and use fewer parameters while achieving comparable performance to LSTMs.

questions.question: In the Query-Key-Value (Q, K, V) formulation of attention, what does the 'Query' represent?
options: The current focus or item actively seeking relevant information
The gradient of the loss function
questions.explanation: The Query represents the current token's request, matched against all Keys to determine attention weights over Values.

questions.question: What is the mathematical equation for Scaled Dot-Product Attention?
options: Attention(Q, K, V) = Q * K * V
Attention(Q, K, V) = Softmax(Q K^T / sqrt(d_k)) * V
Attention(Q, K, V) = Sigmoid(Q + K) / V
Attention(Q, K, V) = ReLU(Q * V) * K
questions.explanation: Scaled dot-product attention computes Softmax(Q K^T / sqrt(d_k)) * V.

questions.question: Unlike RNNs, the Transformer architecture can process all tokens in an input sequence in parallel.
questions.explanation: True. Transformers dispense with sequential recurrence, enabling massive GPU parallelism during training.

questions.question: Because standard Self-Attention is permutation-invariant and has no intrinsic notion of word order, what is added to input token embeddings?
questions.explanation: Positional encodings inject numerical signals indicating the sequential order and relative distance of tokens.

questions.question: What is the purpose of 'Multi-Head Attention' in a Transformer?
options: To train multiple separate models on different computers
To allow the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions
questions.explanation: Multiple heads project Q, K, and V into distinct subspaces, capturing syntactic, semantic, and coreference dependencies simultaneously.

questions.question: The seminal 2017 paper that introduced the Transformer architecture is titled 'Attention Is All You ______'.
questions.explanation: Vaswani et al.'s 2017 paper was titled 'Attention Is All You Need'.

questions.question: In Self-Attention, the Query, Key, and Value vectors are all linear projections of the same sequence of tokens.
questions.explanation: True. In self-attention, each input token projects into Q, K, and V through separate learned weight matrices.

questions.question: What is the computational time and memory complexity of standard Self-Attention with respect to sequence length N?
questions.explanation: Comparing every token to every other token requires an N x N attention matrix, giving quadratic O(N^2) complexity.

questions.question: What is the function of a 'Causal Attention Mask' in autoregressive Transformer decoders (like GPT)?
options: To prevent tokens from attending to future tokens that appear later in the sequence
To hide training data from hackers
questions.explanation: Causal masking sets upper-triangle attention scores to -infinity, ensuring predictions at step t only depend on known past tokens 1..t.

questions.question: Which famous Transformer model was designed as a bidirectional encoder trained on Masked Language Modeling (filling missing blanks)?
questions.explanation: BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) trains an encoder bidirectionally using masked language modeling.

questions.question: Layer Normalization in Transformers normalizes across features for each individual token independently of other batch elements.
questions.explanation: True. Unlike Batch Normalization, LayerNorm computes statistics across hidden dimensions per token, making it ideal for variable length sequences.

questions.question: What technique allows modern Transformer models to scale context windows to 100,000+ tokens efficiently?
options: FlashAttention (IO-aware tiling) and Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE)
questions.explanation: FlashAttention avoids materializing massive N x N attention matrices in GPU HBM via fast SRAM tiling, unlocking huge contexts.
